# Below-OC cap budgets can have strict negative constrained curvature

The menu in this note has genuinely smaller masses than the OC target, and its original body is an actual global fixed-cap volume maximizer within its fixed planar normal fan. All compatibility constraints are retained. Nevertheless a nonzero parity-neutral volume-positive velocity has strictly negative full Lagrangian curvature. This proves that small cap budgets alone do not exclude cap-curvature cancellation.

The crucial limitation is explicit: this is NOT a critical cap cover. Its caps miss the common fiber centroid and do not cover the original mixed set. Thus it does not refute OC or a second-order statement which additionally uses actual through-source critical incidence and coverage.

## 1. Exact global inequality for one aligned triangle

Let

    T=conv{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)},  |T|=9/2,
    u1=(1,0), u2=(0,1), u3=(-1,-1).

Every positive triangle with this fixed outward normal fan is uniquely c+rT with r>0 and c in R². The vectors u_i are the three opposite, vertex-cap normals; they sum to zero and span R².

Fix 0<epsilon<=1, put t=2-epsilon, and keep the three halfplanes

    H_i={x:u_i.x>=t}

fixed throughout every variation. Define C_i(c,r)=|(c+rT) intersect H_i|. With

    a_i=2r+u_i.c-t,

the exact cap formula, including every boundary status, is

    C_i(c,r) = (1/2) min{max(a_i,0),3r}².                (1)

Indeed a_i<=0 gives an empty or tangent vertex section. For 0<a_i<3r, the cut removes a right triangular vertex cap with both edge-coordinate lengths a_i and area a_i²/2. For a_i>=3r it contains the whole triangle of area (3r)²/2. The formulas agree at both endpoints; closed lines have zero planar area.

Since sum_i a_i=6r-3t, (1) implies

    sum_i C_i(c,r)
      >= min{(9/2)r², (3/2)(2r-t)_+²}.                 (2)

If some a_i>=3r, its one full cap proves the first alternative. Otherwise every cap equals a_i,+²/2, and Cauchy–Schwarz gives sum a_i,+² >= (sum a_i)_+²/3, proving the second. No cut-status hypothesis has been omitted.

Set lambda=3/(2epsilon)>1 and L0=(9/4)(2-epsilon). Then the GLOBAL inequality

    |c+rT|-lambda sum_i C_i(c,r) <= L0                (3)

holds for every r>0 and c. Equality holds only at r=1,c=0.

To prove it, subtract lambda times the lower bound (2). The resulting upper bound is the maximum of

    (1-lambda)(9/2)r²,
    (9/2)r²-(3lambda/2)(2r-t)_+².

The first is nonpositive, hence strictly below L0. For r>=t/2 the second is exactly

    L0-[9(2-epsilon)/(2epsilon)](r-1)².              (4)

For 0<r<=t/2 it is (9/2)r², whose maximum on that interval is strictly below L0: the difference at r=t/2 is (9/8)epsilon(2-epsilon)>0. Thus equality forces r=1 and equality in the Cauchy–Schwarz step. All a_i are then equal to epsilon>0, so u_i.c=0 for all i and c=0. Conversely this triangle has three proper caps of area epsilon²/2 and attains equality in (3).

## 2. An actual globally maximizing mixed family with below-target budgets

Take n=1,d=2 and the genuine product convex body

    C=[0,2] times T.

Its COMPLETE integer fibers are T at bases 0,1,2. Thus M=27/2. Use the three cylindrical ambient caps

    {(z,x):u_i.x>=2-epsilon}, i=1,2,3.

Every cap has actual mixed area

    Q=3epsilon²/2 < 3 = (Gamma_2/2)M,
    Gamma_2=4/9.                                           (5)

All three cuts are proper on every original fiber. The continuous normals form a positive full-rank circuit, with the same original fixed planes throughout the optimization. All three fiber areas 9/2 are strictly below M/2=27/4.

Consider ALL actual compatible positive triangle families over the same complete base {0,1,2}, with the same fixed outward fan, subject to these three total cap budgets <=Q. Write their fibers as c_j+r_jT. Summing (3) gives

    M' <= lambda sum_(i=1)^3 C_i(total)+3L0
       <= 3lambda Q+3L0
       = 27/2.                                             (6)

Therefore the original product body is an actual GLOBAL volume maximizer for this constrained problem. Equality forces every fiber to be exactly T, so the maximizer is unique in these support coordinates. The proof allowed every compatible variation simultaneously and did not optimize fibers separately under artificial individual cap constraints.

## 3. A genuine parity-neutral compatible velocity

For small signed s vary the actual fibers by

    r_0(s)=1-s, r_1(s)=1, r_2(s)=1+s, c_j(s)=0.          (7)

The radii are affine in the base coordinate, so their convex hull has exactly these integer fibers; every midpoint compatibility inequality remains equality. This is an actual two-sided support velocity, not a relaxation of the active support cone.

The radius velocity (-1,0,1) sums to zero separately on the even bases {0,2} and the odd base {1}. Accordingly, the first total-volume derivative, every first cap derivative, and those derivatives summed separately within each parity class all vanish. In the nearby proper-cut chamber the exact polynomials are

    M(s)=27/2+9s²,
    C_i(total;s)=3epsilon²/2+4s², i=1,2,3.              (8)

Thus the raw volume Hessian is strictly positive:

    M''(0)=18.

But the FULL normalized Lagrangian Hessian is

    [M-lambda sum_i C_i]''(0)
      =18-24lambda
      =18-36/epsilon <0.                               (9)

For epsilon=1 its value is -18. The normal first-order stress with common multiplier lambda is exact on all simultaneous fixed-fan support variations: at every original fiber, the center derivatives cancel because sum u_i=0, while the radius derivative is 9=6epsilon lambda. Compatibility stress is zero, although active compatibility constraints are still present and (7) preserves them.

Equation (6) ensures that no acceleration can convert this velocity into a budget-feasible volume gain. The negative curvature is therefore a real constrained obstruction, rather than an artifact of a merely stationary point.

## 4. What the certificate excludes

The numerical premise Q<(Gamma_2/2)M is true, and can hold with an arbitrarily small ratio Q/M=epsilon²/9. It does not imply that weighted fixed-cap Hessians are dominated by the total volume Hessian on parity-neutral velocities. Equations (8)–(9) give the opposite strict inequality at a genuine global maximum.

What fails is the through-source critical-cover premise: 2-epsilon>0, so all three caps miss the original point (j,0) in every fiber. Their boundaries do not meet at any common continuous point because their equal positive thresholds have sum 3(2-epsilon), whereas sum u_i=0. They cannot be substituted for a critical circuit at a fiber maximum or for the full-fiber critical cover in `candidate b989614dc4f86228`.

Consequently a valid below-target spectral argument must use this missing critical incidence or the full covering geometry in addition to the exact small budgets. The example does not establish that such an additional argument is impossible.
